name: Question 4
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{3},3{t}^{2}-6t⟩,$ find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector $⟨1,-4⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-6t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{t}^{2},6t-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $⟨1,-4⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $⟨1,-4⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨1,-4⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨1,-4⟩\cdot ⟨6{t}^{2},6t-6⟩ & =0 \\ 1(6{t}^{2})+(-4)(6t-6) & =0 \\ 6{t}^{2}-24t+24 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-4t+4 & =0 \\ (t-2)^{2} & =0 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only solution is $t=2.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =⟨2(2)^{3},3(2)^{2}-6(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨16,0⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨1,-4⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(16,0).$

Question 4
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨2t3,3t2−6t⟩, find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector ⟨1,−4⟩.

a
(−8,2)
b
(−2,0) and (2,0)
c
(4,2) and (16,0)
d
(4,2)
e
(16,0)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative of r(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(2t3),ddt(3t2−6t)⟩=⟨6t2,6t−6⟩

The vectors ⟨1,−4⟩ and r′(t) are perpendicular for some value of the parameter t if and only if ⟨1,−4⟩⋅r′(t)=0. So, we have ⟨1,−4⟩⋅r′(t)=0⟨1,−4⟩⋅⟨6t2,6t−6⟩=01(6t2)+(−4)(6t−6)=06t2−24t+24=0t2−4t+4=0(t−2)2=0t=2.

Therefore, the only solution is t=2.

Finally, since r(2)=⟨2(2)3,3(2)2−6(2)⟩=⟨16,0⟩, we conclude that ⟨1,−4⟩ and r′(t) are perpendicular at the point (16,0).
